messages:

Subject: Post-call recap & next steps — Novapay pricing discussion

Alex — great to meet earlier. Quick recap from our 45-min discovery so we have alignment and a clear next step: 

What I heard:
- Primary use: customer support automation and inbox summarization; average response length ~120 tokens, bursts of longer summaries (~800 tokens) for weekly digests.
- Expected Q3 volumes: 50M tokens/month baseline, with 150M tokens/month peak during campaigns.
- Data posture: PII redaction required, SOC2 scope, likely Dedicated or Private if we move forward.
- Budget: Erica indicated an initial target range of $12k–$20k/month for inference costs (we discussed unit economics and total TCO).

Action items I volunteered:
1) Put together an invoice-level cost estimate + model cost breakdown for your volumes (attached cost model workbook).
2) Suggest configurations (batching, KV cache policy, quantization profile) to get to your target $/1M tokens.
3) Introduce procurement if we need to get an SOW or billing terms.

Next step: I'll send an initial invoice estimate and a short note on tradeoffs (latency vs. unit cost). Can you confirm the 50M baseline / 150M peak numbers and whether you expect the usage to be fairly steady vs. seasonal spikes?

Thanks — talk soon.

--
Sean Gallagher
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.com

From: Alex Johnson <alex@novapay.com>

Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 17:03:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & next steps — Novapay pricing discussion

Sean — thanks for the recap and the quick turnaround. Confirming numbers: baseline 50M tokens/month, peak 150M tokens/month during promos (3–4 month windows). The 50M baseline is what we need to plan for.

A couple of clarifications:
- Of the baseline, ~60% will be short completions (<=200 tokens), 40% will be embeddings/longer summaries (~600–800 tokens) used for search/rerank and weekly digests.
- Our procurement lead (procurement@novapay.com) will want a PDF estimate to attach to the initial budget request.
- Erica: our target is to keep unit inference spend below ~$2500 per 1M tokens effective OSS cost (before infra & support) — I know that’s aggressive, but that’s the internal budget target.

Appreciate the model — look forward to the invoice estimate.

Alex
Director of Product
Novapay

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex@novapay.com>, procurement@novapay.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2027 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Invoice estimate + cost breakdown (attached)

Alex / Procurement — attaching a concise invoice estimate (PDF) and the cost model workbook (XLSX). Highlights up-front so you can share with budget owners: 

High-level invoice estimate (monthly, US region, Redwood Hosted API pricing assumptions):
- Baseline (50M tokens/month): estimated invoice = $13,800/month
  - Generation (30M tokens @ model-gen profile): $8,400
  - Embeddings & Rerank (20M tokens): $3,600
  - Networking & misc: $1,800
- Peak (150M tokens/month, routing + burst capacity): estimated invoice = $36,600/month

Unit economics and target $/1M tokens (what I used in the model):
- Effective invoice target for Novapay: ~$276 per 1M tokens (this is Redwood invoice cost given current promo/commit pricing assumptions in the workbook).
- On raw model compute (without caching or batching), a standard gen model at 8-bit quantization would be ~ $1,500 – $2,000 per 1M tokens equivalent on dedicated infra. The difference is the platform, caching, and amortized infra assumptions.

Key levers to reach Erica's internal budget target (~$2,500 / 1M tokens stated as target in your note):
1) Quantization + model selection: choose a quantized compatible model (we show alternatives in the sheet) — can reduce per-token compute by ~2–3x vs full fp16.
2) Prefix/KV caching for chat-heavy use: for repeated prompts we estimate 20–30% token reuse.
3) Batching policy tuning: aggressive batching for async workloads yields 15–25% marginal savings.
4) Reserved capacity (Dedicated) commit: with a 12-month commit we can bring the effective per-1M invoice closer to your target (see commit bands in the sheet).

Attached files: novapay_cost_model.xlsx — tabs include assumptions, line-item invoice, commit scenarios, sensitivity by token mix; redwood_invoice_estimate_20270601.pdf — a one-page estimate you can share with procurement.

If helpful, I can run two scenarios: (A) Hosted API + cache/batching optimizations (fastest time-to-value) and (B) Dedicated reserved pool (12mo) with committed discounts and quantized model. Which would you prefer to see first?

Best,
Sean

[Attachment: novapay_cost_model.xlsx (34 KB)]

Sean — copying a quick note for the deal playbook before we pass to Solutions/SE for tuning: 
- For Novapay volumes (50–150M), start with Hosted API scenario A, iterate on batching + caching for 2–4 weeks to validate effective $/1M. If simulated effective cost > target, propose Dedicated 12mo commit with quantization.
- Flagging that procurement will ask about SOC2 evidence + data residency; include Private deployment pricing as a follow-up.

Also — can you include a quick sensitivity for token mix (20/80 vs 60/40 gen vs embed) in the workbook? It helps procurement see worst/best case.

Marissa
Senior Sales Ops, Redwood Inference

Sean / Marissa — thanks, this is helpful. Procurement has what it needs for a first pass (PDF attached to our internal ticket).

I reviewed the workbook quickly — can you run the two scenarios you suggested and send separate one-page comparisons? Specifically we want: 
- Scenario A: Hosted API with caching & batching optimizations (assume 25% cache hit for chat, 20% batching savings)
- Scenario B: Dedicated 12mo commit, quantized model, same usage profile

If Scenario B hits the eco target of <= $2,500 / 1M effective for our observed token mix, we'll start a procurement discussion. Please shoot those one-pagers by end of day Friday so I can share with Erica.

Alex
